info.title: England Orders — Staff App API
info.description:
API behind the England Orders staff app (internal team, admin accounts). Source of truth: fmcg_orders, fmcg_customers, fmcg_order_items; the app writes only fmcg_order_deliveries (delivery date, Pandi, Adda, Builty images). No prices are returned. Order status, quantities, prices and stock are never changed.

Every response uses one envelope (same as the Masoom app API): `{error, message, code, data}`; `code` equals the HTTP status; failures carry a stable `data.reason` (and `data.fields` for validation). Examples are real responses captured from the local test server (tokens/signatures redacted).

**Accountrix ERP sales (v1.3).** Posted ERP sales are listed with website orders. The England backend pulls them from the ERP's read-only feed (`GET {ERP}/api/integrations/england/sales`, server-to-server bearer token, never sent to the app) into `fmcg_erp_sales` — one row per ERP sale (unique `erp_sale_id`), keeping the ERP invoice number, customer, date and net total. ERP sales are NOT copied into fmcg_orders and the ERP is never written. Every list card and detail carries `origin` (`website` | `erp`) and a unique `key` (`web-<id>` / `erp-<id>`); ids are only unique within one origin, so ERP records are opened via `/app/erp-sales/{id}`. Delivery date, Pandi, Adda and Builty images for an ERP sale are stored in England's `fmcg_erp_sale_deliveries`.

Examples come from the local integration rig (TEST records created through the real website order service and the real ERP SaleService). Ids in your database will differ: take them from `GET /app/orders`.

**Mixed ERP invoices (v1.3).** The ERP feed sends only the configured company's (England) lines and counts the rest (`other_company_lines`); the feed stays off until `ENGLAND_SYNC_COMPANY_IDS` is set in the ERP.

get.summary: Website orders and ERP sales, customer-wise cards (no prices)
get.description: Website orders (fmcg_orders + fmcg_customers + fmcg_order_items) and Accountrix ERP sales (fmcg_erp_sales) in one list. Each card has `origin`, `key`, customer name/phone/city, Adda/Pandi, every product with quantity and unit, and the Builty status. No prices on cards (the total is on the detail screen). Tabs use the effective date — delivery date, else order date — in Asia/Karachi; a saved delivery date is never overwritten. `tab=all` lists everything. Sort: newest first (previous: latest effective date first). Calling this also refreshes ERP sales when the last refresh is older than `ERP_SYNC_SECONDS` (default 60 s); if the ERP is unreachable the last copied sales are still returned and `data.sources.erp.ok` is false.

post.summary: Upload / replace the front or back Builty image

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: fmcg_orders.id — take it from `data.orders[].id` where `origin` is `website`.

post.description: multipart/form-data. The image is saved ONLY to this order: order_code must equal the order's code (else 409, nothing stored). Validation: JPG, PNG or WebP; max 10 MB (FMCG_SLIP_MAX_KB); shortest usable edge ≥ 200 px; images larger than 2400 px are scaled down (needs GD). Files are stored outside the web root. On replace the previous file of that side is deleted only after the new one is saved; if the database save fails the new file is removed (no orphans). Throttled 30/min.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: fmcg_erp_sales.id — take it from `data.orders[].id` where `origin` is `erp` (NOT the ERP's own sale id; that is `erp.sale_id`).

get.description: `code` is the ERP invoice number. `erp` holds the values as typed on the ERP invoice. `pandi_name` / `adda_name` show the value saved in the app, else the ERP value (`pandi_from_erp` / `adda_from_erp` = true). `total` is the ERP net total (read-only). Mixed invoices (England items plus other companies' items): only the England lines are listed; `erp.other_company_lines` says how many other-company lines the invoice also has. `total` is always the ERP net total of the WHOLE invoice (`total_scope: whole_invoice`) — line prices are not copied, so there is no England-only amount. The ERP invoice is never changed.
